pins.title: Gifts a hiker will actually use
pins.sub: Ideas for every budget, many under $25.
pins.pinTitle: Gifts for hikers under $25: wool socks, a headlamp, a trail map and other ideas they will use
pins.description: The best gifts for hikers get used on every hike: merino socks, a rechargeable headlamp, a sit pad, a paper map of their home park or a hike together. Our gift guide sorts practical ideas by budget, from free to about $80, and says what not to buy as a surprise.

pins.title: Collect every park you visit
pins.sub: State parks passport and national parks tracker.
pins.board: Best Day Hikes in US National Parks
pins.pinTitle: Parks passport printable: state parks passport and all 64 US national parks tracker in one gift
pins.description: For hikers who collect parks: a printable State Parks Passport for all 50 states and Canada's provinces, plus the US National Parks Hiking Tracker with all 64 parks. Visit logs and stamp boxes for every trip. Instant PDF download, an easy gift for park lovers.

pins.title: Give them a year of hiking goals
pins.sub: Planner, peak logbook and parks tracker.
pins.pinTitle: 2027 hiking goals gift set printable: year planner, hike-a-week challenge, peak logbook and parks tracker
pins.description: A gift for the hiker making plans for next year: the 2027 Hiking Year Planner with the 52-hike challenge, the Peak Bagger's Logbook and the US National Parks Tracker. Three printables in one instant download, so you can give it the same day.

pins.title: 40°F and frosty? Dress in layers.
pins.sub: What to wear, from base layer to hat.
pins.pinTitle: What to wear hiking in 40 degree weather: layers, jacket, hat and gloves for a cold morning hike
pins.description: At 40°F (4°C) you start cold and warm up fast on the climb. Wear a base layer that wicks sweat, a fleece you can take off and a wind shell, plus a hat and light gloves. Our guide covers each layer and what to avoid, like cotton.

pins.title: The Smokies are quieter in winter
pins.sub: Plan the hikes, drives and parking.
pins.pinTitle: Great Smoky Mountains trip planner printable: itineraries, best hikes, parking tags and seasons
pins.description: Planning a trip to the Great Smoky Mountains? Our printable guide covers when to go, 3, 5 and 7-day itineraries built around the best day hikes, and the parking tag rules. Winter brings fewer crowds, but some roads close: always check nps.gov/grsm before you go.

pins.title: Hiking with your dog this winter?
pins.sub: A checklist for both of you.
pins.pinTitle: Hiking with your dog printable guide: dog hiking checklist, trail etiquette and cold-weather tips
pins.description: A printable guide for hiking with your dog: building up distance, water and paw care, trail manners, heat and cold, where dogs are allowed, plus a dog first aid checklist and pack lists. Instant PDF download with checklists you can print for every trip.

pins.title: Gift for a national park road-tripper
pins.pinTitle: National park trip planner bundle printable: Smoky Mountains, Utah Mighty 5 and Yellowstone guides
pins.description: Three printable national park trip planners in one gift: the Great Smoky Mountains, Utah's Mighty 5 and Yellowstone with Grand Teton. Itineraries, best day hikes and what to book ahead. Instant download, so it works as a last-minute gift.

pins.title: Air-dry your merino socks
pins.sub: Skip the hot dryer, they last longer.
pins.pinTitle: How to wash merino wool socks so they last: inside out, cool wash, dry flat
pins.description: Merino socks last longer with a little care: wash them inside out on a cool wool cycle or by hand, skip the bleach and the tumble dryer, and dry them flat. Ours are 80% merino as labelled, cushioned crew socks for cold days at home, at work and outdoors. Sold as one pair.

pins.title: Wet day? Warm feet anyway.
pins.sub: Merino stays warm even when damp.
pins.pinTitle: Merino wool socks for wet, cold days: warm even when damp, on the trail, the commute and dog walks
pins.description: Puddles, slush and wet trails: cotton socks feel cold once they get damp, merino keeps its warmth. Our cushioned crew socks are 80% merino as labelled, for rainy commutes, dog walks and winter hikes. Sold as one pair, in four colours.

pins.title: Water bottle freezing? Carry it upside down.
pins.sub: Ice forms at the base, not the lid.
pins.pinTitle: How to keep water from freezing on a winter hike: upside-down bottles, warm water and insulation
pins.description: Water bottles freeze from the top down, so the lid ices up first. Carry bottles upside down with a lid that seals well, start with warm water, keep them inside your pack and blow your drink tube clear after every sip. Seven simple tricks in our guide.
